extracted.intended_audience: inventors and patent applicants (including pro se applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing a U.S. utility patent application (including related provisional guidance), covering required sections, formal requirements, claim drafting, drawings, and enablement/description standards. Aimed at helping inventors produce a compliant specification and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of a patent application disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application disclosure should include a Detailed Description, Drawing, Abstract, and Claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the principal components to capture the invention; ensure each is present and properly organized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement requirement (35 U.S.C. §112)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must contain a written description of the invention and of the manner and process of making and using it, in full, clear, concise, and exact terms so as to enable any person skilled in the art to make and use the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enablement is required for both provisional and nonprovisional disclosures; the detailed description must allow practice without undue experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be supported by the disclosure at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations of claims can be modified based only on the disclosed invention at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture the invention using clear and consistent language throughout the disclosure so claim terms find antecedent basis in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear and consistent language throughout the disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Important to capture the invention using clear and consistent language throughout the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft terminology deliberately (drafting claims first is recommended) to ensure terms used in claims are supported and consistently used in the specification and drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional applications are not examined or published, have a one-year time limit, and are only for utility inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications automatically abandon after one year; no claims are required, but the written disclosure must meet the same requirements as a nonprovisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprovisional application characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprovisional applications are examined, require at least one claim, must meet written description/enablement requirements (35 U.S.C. §112), and are generally published 18 months from earliest filing date unless non-publication is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonprovisional applications can result in an issued patent; follow formal filing requirements and prepare claims carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application filing/legal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional filing must clearly indicate that a provisional application is being filed, include payment of the fee, a description enabling someone to make and use the invention, and drawings if necessary to understand the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PTO/SB/16 (cover sheet) or otherwise make the provisional status clear; include sufficient disclosure to support later nonprovisional claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional cover sheet required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisional cover sheet should include inventor name(s), inventor residence(s), title of the invention, correspondence address, attorney information (if any), and U.S. government interest (if any).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete administrative data to avoid filing defects; use the prescribed form for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprovisional filing package requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional utility patent application must include a specification (description and claim(s)), drawings when necessary, an oath or declaration, and prescribed filing, search, and examination fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow USPTO guidance/online resources and include all required components to avoid processing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification purpose and basic requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification is the written description of the invention and how to make and use it; it must be in clear, full, concise, and exact terms to allow a person skilled in the art to make and use the invention and must include at least one specific embodiment and conclude with at least one claim (on a new page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the specification gives practical instructions and includes at least one concrete embodiment (preferably the best mode known).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification page format
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification, abstract and claims must be 1.5 or double-spaced in a single column, written on one side in portrait orientation, on 8.5x11 inch paper with margins (¾ inches all around except left margin at least 1 inch), pages numbered consecutively starting with page one, and use a nonscript font (e.g., Arial, Times Roman, Courier), preferably 12 point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to these formatting rules to meet USPTO filing standards and avoid processing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification sections (required/typical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical sections include Title of the Invention; Background; Brief Summary of the Invention; Brief Description of the Drawings; Detailed Description of the Invention; Claims (on a separate sheet); and Abstract (less than 150 words, one paragraph, on a separate sheet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the specification with these sections in mind; ensure the abstract and claims are on separate sheets as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesser-used specification sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Cross Reference to Related Applications, Statement Regarding Federally Sponsored Research, Names of Parties to a Joint Research Agreement, Incorporation by Reference of material submitted via compact disk or text file, Statement Regarding Prior Disclosure by the Inventor, and Sequence Listing where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these only when applicable (e.g., continuations, federally funded work, sequence listings) and follow proper formatting and content rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of the invention guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should be as specific as possible, avoid generic language such as 'system and method for ...', and allow a reader to readily ascertain what the invention is; the title may be changed by the examiner at allowance if not satisfactory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think of the title as a quick description; use clear, specific wording but note it can be changed during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract must start on a separate sheet with the heading 'Abstract', be 150 words or less, 1.5 or double-spaced, narrative form in a single paragraph, point out what is new in the technology, not repeat the claims or brief summary, and be written to enable the public to quickly determine the nature of the technical disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the abstract concise and focused on what is novel; do not restate claim language as the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background of the invention content
rubrics_metrics.description: Background should describe the field of the invention at a high level, related art (what you know has been done before), and the problems that led you to come up with your invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the context and problems addressed by the invention but avoid personal stories of conception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief summary of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief summary always precedes the Detailed Description and should apprise the public and artisans of the nature of the invention with one or more clear, concise sentences or paragraphs directed to the specific invention being claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistency between the summary and the subject matter of the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of the drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: If drawings are part of the application, include a brief statement of what each figure depicts (e.g., front view, expanded view) before the application is considered complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each figure by number and briefly describe what it shows; mention each figure separately when labeled (e.g., 1A, 1B, 1C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings as disclosure and filing timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are part of the disclosure and are required if necessary to understand the invention; a drawing necessary to understand the invention cannot be introduced after the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include drawings that show every feature of the claimed invention and submit them with the filing to preserve priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must show every feature of the invention claimed and contain as many views as necessary to show the invention; drawings are deemed acceptable/unacceptable based on readability and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient views and detail to allow clear understanding of the claimed features; unreadable drawings can be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing technical/form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer black and white line drawings with lines and numbers heavy enough for adequate reproduction; color drawings are permitted; photographs may be accepted in special circumstances; use reference characters (numerals preferred); each figure must be labeled (e.g., FIG. 1); avoid using descriptive words in the figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent reference numerals (each numeral for only one part) and avoid text inside figures that attempts to describe structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The detailed description should explain the invention and the process of making and using it in full, clear, concise and exact terms, focusing on structures, processes or compositions, and should refer to the figures explaining parts by reference numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the most important part of the application; provide specific detail and link claim terms to clear embodiments and figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear support/antecedent basis for claim terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The detailed description should provide clear support or antecedent basis for all terms used in the claims so the meaning of claim terms is ascertainable by reference to the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft claims first if helpful; use the claims as a checklist to ensure the description supports all claimed terms and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification DOs (recommended practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the invention clearly to allow any person skilled in the art to make and use the invention without undue experimentation; ensure each reference numeral is used for only one part and mentioned in the specification; provide at least one specific embodiment including the best known to you at filing; include a Brief Description of the Drawings that names each figure; provide proper antecedent basis for all claim terms; focus on technical features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these practices to strengthen compliance with written description and enablement requirements and to reduce prosecution issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification cautions (what to avoid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use trademarks in the title or to describe structure; Background need not state how the inventor conceived the invention; avoid claims of future commercial success (e.g., 'will sell and make millions'); do not include detailed discussion of the figures or refer to reference characters in the Brief Description of the Drawings; proofread for grammatical errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid non-technical, promotional, or improperly placed content that may confuse the scope or sufficiency of disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim support rule: 'If it is in the claim, it must be in the specification'
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims define the invention and what aspects are legally enforceable; they must conform to the invention as set forth in the remainder of the specification and claim terms must find clear support/antecedent basis in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every claimed limitation has textual support in the specification to withstand written description challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and formal requirements of claim(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must start on a separate sheet with the heading 'Claim Listing', be 1.5 or double spaced, each claim be a single sentence (begin with a capital letter and end with a period), have numbering preserved throughout prosecution, and applicants may file up to 3 independent claims and 20 total claims before excess claim fees apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow formatting rules, observe claim count limitations to anticipate fees, and preserve original numbering during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. patent claim statutory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional patent application must have at least one claim that particularly points out and distinctly defines the invention; claims may be written in independent or dependent form, and a dependent claim incorporates by reference all limitations of the claim to which it refers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clear claims that distinctly point out the invention; use dependent claims to add limitations and fallback positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions to answer before drafting claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to writing claims, determine: What is the invention? What are the pieces and parts that make up the invention? How do the pieces and parts relate to one another? Do you have more than one invention (tangible vs method)? Are there multiple versions of each invention?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these questions to decompose the invention and plan claim scope and claim sets (apparatus, method, composition) appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Think strategically to obtain the broadest valid claim possible and claims with a variety of claim scope, not just at time of filing but during prosecution; consider whether some claims filed are likely to be patentable without amendment and the implications of provisional rights (35 U.S.C. §154(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File a mix of broad and narrower claims to maximize protection and immediate enforceability; plan for prosecution amendments and provisional priority where applicable.
